funFacts: The Rolex Shanghai Masters returns as Asia's sole ATP Masters 1000 event, featuring an expanded 96-player singles draw across 12 days.
Carlos Alcaraz arrives in Shanghai riding a nine-match winning streak following back-to-back tournament triumphs at the Laver Cup and China Open in Beijing.
Novak Djokovic returns to Shanghai competing for an unprecedented fifth title, having previously lifted the trophy in 2012, 2013, 2015, and 2018.

headline: Rolex Shanghai Masters: ATP 1000 main draw kicks off with Alcaraz, Sinner, and Djokovic eyeing Asian hardcourt glory
whyCareReason: The premier ATP Masters 1000 tournament in Asia gets underway at Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena with 1,000 ranking points and the battle for year-end world No. 1 on the line.

story:
Why this one matters: Just twenty-four hours after Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner staged a 3h21m masterpiece in Beijing, the epicenter of men's tennis shifts 800 miles south to the futuristic Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena for the Rolex Shanghai Masters.

As the eighth ATP Masters 1000 event of the calendar, Shanghai offers 1,000 crucial ranking points in the ATP Race to Turin. Sinner enters as the top seed, seeking immediate redemption after falling in Sunday's deciding tiebreak. Alcaraz arrives brimming with momentum, riding a nine-match winning streak that includes crowns at the Laver Cup and China Open.

Adding immense intrigue to the field is four-time Shanghai champion Novak Djokovic, who makes his much-anticipated return to Chinese soil aiming for his 41st career Masters 1000 title. With early-round clashes featuring veterans like Stan Wawrinka and Kei Nishikori alongside rising stars, Shanghai promises twelve days of world-class drama.
stakes: 1,000 ATP ranking points, a 1.1 million dollar winner's check, and critical positioning in the race for year-end World No. 1.
rivalryAngle: Sinner and Alcaraz could meet for the fourth time in 2026, while Djokovic lurks on Alcaraz's side of the draw in a potential semifinal blockbuster.
